html:
The Siege of Khartoum lasted from March 1884 to 26 January 1885, when the forces of the Mahdi stormed the city and killed its governor, the British general Charles Gordon.

Gordon had been sent to evacuate the Egyptian garrison as the rising of the Mahdi swept the country, but he chose to hold the city. A British relief force sent up the Nile arrived two days after the city fell.

The death of Gordon made him a Christian martyr in British eyes and a public scandal for Prime Minister Gladstone. The Mahdi died months later, and his successor, the Khalifa Abdallahi, ruled the Mahdist state from Omdurman until the Battle of Omdurman. The siege ended Egyptian rule in Sudan.
sum: The Siege of Khartoum lasted from March 1884 to 26 January 1885, when the forces of the Mahdi stormed the city and killed its governor, the British general Charles Gordon.
